mainTopic: A parallel מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about a tree that sprouts from an old trunk or roots (in ערלה), why both disputes are needed, and how far the upper garden owner may reach under רבי שמעון's rule in the משנה.
overview: The גמרא first brings a ברייתא about ערלה in which רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue about new growth from an old tree's trunk or roots, just as they argued earlier about who owns such growth. It then explains why both disputes had to be taught: money cases and איסור cases could be judged differently. Next it returns to רבי שמעון's rule in the משנה about the upper and lower gardens. דבי רבי ינאי add that the upper owner only gets what he can reach without straining. רב ענן, or רבי ירמיה, asks what happens if the owner can reach only the leaves or only the root, and the question ends as תיקו. ריש לקיש rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון, and שבור מלכא praises the ruling as fair. The amud closes with the הדרן, ending the פרק and all of מסכת בבא מציעא.

steps.title: The same dispute appears about ערלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a parallel ברייתא: a tree sprouting from an old trunk or roots is subject to ערלה according to רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה exempts growth from the trunk and obligates growth from the roots.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned a case just like this about ערלה: a tree that grows out of the trunk or the roots of an old tree must keep ערלה, says רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: if it grew from the trunk it is exempt, but if it grew from the roots it must keep ערלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue in the same way in a second area, the laws of ערלה. This sets up the next step, which explains why both disputes are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats any new sprout, from the trunk or the roots, as a brand-new tree, so the ערלה years start again. רבי יהודה sees a sprout from the trunk as just a branch of the old tree. A sprout from the roots, though, counts as a new tree for him. This is the same split they had in the earlier ownership case.

keyTerms.meaning: The ban on eating a tree's fruit during its first three years
The trunk of a tree
Roots
Like this, in the same way
Obligated / exempt

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי עָרְלָה כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא:
phrases.english: And we also learned regarding ערלה a case like this:
phrases.notes: "Like this" points back to the earlier argument about who owns a tree that sprouts from an old trunk or roots.

phrases.aramaic: אִילָן הַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַגֶּזַע וּמִן הַשָּׁרָשִׁין –
phrases.english: A tree that comes out from the trunk and from the roots
phrases.notes: This means a new shoot growing out of an old tree that was cut down.

phrases.english: is obligated in ערלה; these are the words of רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מִן הַגֶּזַע – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: רבי יהודה says: from the trunk, it is exempt;
from the roots, it is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי גַּבֵּי עָרְלָה כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel source to the earlier ownership dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a sprout from the trunk or the roots is a new tree for ערלה. רבי יהודה: from the trunk it is exempt, from the roots it is obligated.

steps.title: Why both disputes had to be taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that both disputes are needed. In a money case רבי יהודה might be lenient but agree to רבי מאיר in an איסור case. In an איסור case רבי מאיר might be strict but agree to רבי יהודה in a money case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we only had the first case, about ownership, we might say רבי יהודה ruled that way only because it is about money, but for ערלה, which is an איסור, he would agree with רבי מאיר. If we only had the ערלה case, we might say רבי מאיר ruled that way only there, but in the money case he would agree with רבי יהודה. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: if the two Rabbis argue the same way in both cases, why teach both? It shows that each case teaches something the other could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the money case alone, we might think רבי יהודה would be stricter in an איסור and side with רבי מאיר. From the ערלה case alone, we might think רבי מאיר's view comes from being strict about איסור, so he would agree with רבי יהודה about money. Having both shows that each one holds his view in both areas.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed; both teachings are necessary (a צריכותא)
Money matters
A matter of prohibition
He agrees with him
The first one, the earlier case

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכותא shows that two cases that look the same each teach something new: money cases and איסור cases can be judged differently.
steps.confusionAlert: In the second half, "בהא" (this) means the ערלה case and "בההיא" (that) means the money case. In the first half, "בהא" meant the money case.

phrases.english: And they are needed, for if it had taught us only the first one:
phrases.notes: "The first one" is the earlier case about who owns the new growth, which is a money question.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם דְּמָמוֹנָא,
phrases.english: in this case רבי יהודה said it, because it is money,
but regarding ערלה, which is a prohibition,
I might say he agrees with רבי מאיר.
And if it had been said only in this case:
in this case רבי מאיר said it,
but in that one,
I might say he agrees with רבי יהודה,
so they are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the parallel ערלה dispute from step 1 is not redundant with the earlier ownership dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something the other cannot
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think רבי יהודה is lenient only in money cases, or that רבי מאיר is strict only in איסור cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each holds his view in both money and איסור cases, so both disputes had to be taught.

steps.title: Quoting רבי שמעון's rule in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the upper and lower gardens. It quotes רבי שמעון: whatever the upper owner can reach by stretching out his hand belongs to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: whatever the upper owner can stretch out his hand and reach, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the words of the משנה so it can explain them. This sets up the clarification of רבי שמעון's rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, plants grow on the wall between a higher garden and a lower one. רבי שמעון splits them: what the upper owner can reach by stretching his hand is his, and the rest belongs to the lower owner. The next steps ask exactly what counts as "can reach."

keyTerms.meaning: The upper one, the owner of the higher garden
To stretch out (his hand)
And so on

phrases.english: רבי שמעון said:
Whatever the upper one can stretch out, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: whatever he can reach by stretching out his hand is his, and the rest goes to the lower owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: כֹּל שֶׁהָעֶלְיוֹן יָכוֹל לִפְשׁוֹט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the tree discussion and opens a new topic: the last line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The upper owner gets whatever he can reach by stretching out his hand.

steps.title: Only a normal reach, without straining
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ינאי add a limit to רבי שמעון's rule. The upper owner gets only what he can reach without forcing himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי say: and only as long as he does not strain himself.
steps.whatsHappening: דבי רבי ינאי explain רבי שמעון's rule more exactly. "Can reach" means a normal stretch of the hand, not straining to get there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this limit, the upper owner could stretch as far as possible and take more of the plants. דבי רבי ינאי say we measure by an easy, normal reach. Anything beyond that belongs to the lower owner.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (students) of רבי ינאי
Only as long as, provided that
He forces himself, strains

phrases.english: The school of רבי ינאי say:
And only as long as he does not strain himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יֵאָנֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the rule of רבי שמעון quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reach that counts is a normal stretch of the hand, without straining.

steps.title: What if he can reach only part of the plant?
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן (or רבי ירמיה) asks about a plant where the upper owner can reach the leaves but not the root, or the root but not the leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן, and some say רבי ירמיה, asked: if he can reach its leaves but not its root, or its root but not its leaves, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about רבי שמעון's rule. Which part of the plant decides whether it is within reach: the leaves or the root?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says the upper owner gets what he can reach, but a plant has two ends. Maybe the leaves count, since that is what he can actually grab. Maybe the root counts, since that is where the plant grows from. The question is which part sets the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question he was unsure about
And some say (it was another רבי)
Its leaves, the top part
Its root, the base of the plant
What (is the law)?

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רַב עָנָן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: רב ענן asked, and some say רבי ירמיה:
If he reaches its leaves but does not reach its root,

phrases.aramaic: מַגִּיעַ לְעִיקָּרוֹ וְאֵין מַגִּיעַ לְנוֹפוֹ, מַאי?
phrases.english: or he reaches its root but does not reach its leaves, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב עָנָן, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a further question about how to measure the reach in רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When only one part of a plant is within reach, does the leaves part or the root part decide who owns it?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, so the question is left as תיקו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot settle רב ענן's question, so it ends with תיקו: the question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source or argument decided the question. The case of a plant only partly within reach is left without a clear ruling in the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is left unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's rule covers what the upper owner reaches normally, without straining. Whether the leaves or the root decides is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question of step 5 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No answer is found to whether reaching the leaves or the root decides, so the question stays open.

steps.title: The הלכה Follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: אפרים ספרא, quoting ריש לקיש, rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in the case of the upper and lower gardens.
steps.simpleTranslation: אפרים ספרא, a student of ריש לקיש, said in the name of ריש לקיש: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling for the case of the two gardens. We follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא quoted רבי שמעון's rule: whatever the upper owner can reach by stretching out his hand is his (Step 3). דבי רבי ינאי limited it to what he can reach without forcing himself (Step 4). Now ריש לקיש says this is the הלכה in practice, even though some smaller details were left as תיקו (Step 6).

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
Scribe or teacher
In the name of. He is passing on someone else's teaching.
A major אמורא, the study partner of רבי יוחנן

steps.whatToRemember: In the case of the upper and lower gardens, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון. The upper owner gets whatever he can reach by stretching out his hand.
steps.confusionAlert: The תיקו in Step 6 does not cancel this ruling. The ruling decides the main argument. The תיקו was only about a narrower case, a plant where he can reach the leaves but not the root, or the root but not the leaves.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns the argument in the משנה into practical law.

phrases.english: Efrayim the scribe said
a student of Reish Lakish
in the name of Reish Lakish:
The halacha follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the open question ends in תיקו, the גמרא gives the final ruling on the main argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון in the case of the upper and lower gardens.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The upper owner may take whatever he can reach by stretching out his hand, without forcing himself.

steps.title: שבור מלכא Praises רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: When the ruling was told to the Persian king שבור מלכא, he praised רבי שמעון's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told this ruling to King שבור. He said to them: Let us give praise to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. Even the Persian king thought רבי שמעון's ruling was fair and praised it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds no new law. It shows that רבי שמעון's rule seems fair even to an outsider. Letting the upper owner take what he can easily reach is a sensible way to settle a dispute between neighbors.

keyTerms.meaning: King Shapur, the Persian king in the time of the אמוראים
Praise, or a gift of honor
Let us bring it, let us give it
Before him, in front of him

phrases.english: They said it before King Shapur,
he said to them:
Let us bring praise to Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story that praises the ruling just given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: King שבור praised רבי שמעון's ruling as fair.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק הבית והעלייה and מסכת בבא מציעא
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the פרק הבית והעלייה and of all of מסכת בבא מציעא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק הבית והעלייה, and מסכת בבא מציעא is complete.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing formula. It ends the last פרק and finishes the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It is a farewell to the פרק and a promise to come back and learn it again. Here it also announces that מסכת בבא מציעא is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the closing farewell to a פרק.
Is completed, is finished
Tractate

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת בבא מציעא ends with the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in the case of the two gardens.

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaBayis VeHaAliyah
phrases.notes: "הבית והעלייה" is the name of this last פרק, taken from its opening words.

phrases.english: and Masechet Bava Metzia is completed

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק and the מסכת after the final ruling and story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק and מסכת בבא מציעא are complete.
